title: Dog and the Ball

before.title: Dog and the Ball
before.text:
Every afternoon, a small dog named Rex played in the park with his owner. His favorite game was chasing a bright yellow ball.

Rex would run as fast as he could, jumping over small rocks and around trees to catch the ball before it stopped rolling.

One day, the ball rolled into a small pond. Rex stopped at the edge, unsure whether to jump in. The water looked cold and a little scary.

His owner smiled and said, "It's okay, Rex. You don't have to go in."

But Rex really wanted his favorite ball back. He took a deep breath and jumped into the water. It was cold, but not too bad.

He swam to the ball, grabbed it with his mouth, and swam back to shore, shaking water everywhere once he climbed out.

His owner laughed and gave him a big hug. "Good job, Rex! You are very brave."

From that day on, Rex was not afraid of water anymore. He even learned to enjoy swimming almost as much as playing with his ball.

after.title: Dog and the Ball
after.text:
Rex was a small dog with a favorite yellow ball. Every afternoon, his owner took him to the park. She threw the ball, and Rex ran after it.

One day, the ball rolled into a pond. Rex stopped beside the water. He wanted his ball, but the pond looked cold.

His owner waited beside him. "You can leave it there, Rex," she said.

Rex put one foot in the water. Then he jumped in and swam to the ball. He held it in his mouth and swam back.

On the grass, Rex shook himself. Water flew onto his owner's shoes. She laughed and picked up the wet ball. Rex stood beside her, ready for another game.

title: A Bird at My Window

before.title: A Bird at My Window
before.text:
Every morning, a small brown bird came to Ken’s window.

The bird sat on the same place and looked inside.

Ken put a little water outside. The bird drank from it.

A few days later, the bird came with another bird.

Then there were three.

Ken did not try to touch them. He only watched.

In spring, one bird brought a small piece of grass in its mouth.

Ken saw it fly to a tree near the house.

Soon he found a tiny nest there.

The birds had been his neighbors all along.

title: Cooking Rice for Two

before.title: Cooking Rice for Two
before.text:
Emi usually cooked only for herself.

One evening, her brother came to visit.

She put rice in the pot and added water.

Then she stopped.

How much rice did two people need?

She called her mother and asked.

Her mother laughed and gave simple advice.

“Make a little more than you think. Leftover rice is useful.”

Emi cooked the rice and made vegetables and eggs.

Her brother arrived while she was setting the table.

They ate slowly and talked about their week.

There was some rice left at the end.

The next morning, Emi used it for breakfast.

Her mother had been right in more than one way.

title: A Day in Ancient Pompeii

before.title: A Day in Ancient Pompeii
before.text:

In the year 79, the mountain burst open. Hot ash and stone covered the town. Many homes, streets, and daily things were hidden under the ground.

Hundreds of years later, people began to uncover them. They found wall art, water pipes, food shops, and gardens.

These finds showed how Roman families lived from day to day. The town is famous because a terrible event ended life there, but it also kept many signs of that life safe for us to study.

before.text:
A donkey, a dog, a cat, and a rooster had grown old. Their owners no longer wanted them, so the four animals left home and took the road toward Bremen.

Night came before they reached the city. They saw a light in a house and looked through the window. Robbers were eating at a table inside. The animals formed a tower, with the donkey below and the rooster above. Then they made one huge sound together.

The frightened robbers ran into the woods. The animals entered, ate, and found warm places to sleep. One robber returned, but the cat scratched him, the dog bit him, the donkey kicked him, and the rooster cried from the roof. He fled again.

The four friends never reached Bremen. They had found food, shelter, and a home together. What looked like weakness when each animal stood alone became strength when their voices and abilities were joined.
